changes_made.explanation: This paper is about Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) with linguistic annotation capabilities, not NLG tasks. While it generates text outputs, the primary task is speech recognition, not natural language generation. The linguistic annotations are aligned with recognized speech rather than being standalone NLG outputs.

Normalized metric names to standard forms and removed 'F1' since the paper specifically uses 'F-value' not 'F1'. All metrics are correctly extracted and used to evaluate the generated outputs (transcriptions and annotations).
No LLMs are used as judges in this paper. The paper was published in 2021 and focuses on Transformer-based ASR models, not LLM-based evaluation.
No human evaluation is conducted in this paper. All evaluation is done using automatic metrics.

overall_notes: This paper is primarily an ASR (Automatic Speech Recognition) paper that extends speech recognition to include linguistic annotations. While it does generate text outputs (transcriptions and annotations), it does not address traditional NLG tasks like text summarization, dialogue generation, etc. The paper focuses on speech-to-text with aligned linguistic information rather than natural language generation from non-speech inputs.
